title: How to enlarge cursor in Safari on Mac: simple steps for better visibility
metaTitle: How to enlarge cursor in Safari on Mac: System Settings Guide
description: Learn how to enlarge cursor on Mac to improve visibility while using Safari. Follow these simple system-wide settings steps for any modern macOS version.
targetKeyword: how to enlarge cursor on mac
intro: To enlarge the cursor in Safari on a Mac, you must adjust the system-wide pointer settings in macOS, as Safari does not have an independent cursor size control. These adjustments apply globally to every application on your computer, ensuring your pointer remains consistent across all your web browsing sessions.
tldr: Open System Settings from the Apple menu.
Navigate to Accessibility and then to Display.
Adjust the Pointer size slider to your preferred level.
Enable Shake mouse pointer to locate for extra visibility.

blocks.text: Why you cannot change the cursor inside Safari

Many users look for a specific setting within the Safari preferences menu to change the appearance or size of their mouse pointer. However, Apple designed macOS to handle input device settings at the system level rather than the application level. This ensures that your cursor behaves predictably whether you are inside a browser, a text editor, or a photo management tool. Because Safari relies on the operating system to render the cursor, any changes you make in System Settings will automatically propagate to Safari without needing a restart.
How to enlarge cursor on Mac via System Settings
Adjusting your pointer size is a straightforward process in modern versions of macOS, including Tahoe, Sequoia, and Sonoma. Follow these steps to customize your experience.

items: Click the Apple menu in the top-left corner of your screen.
Select System Settings from the dropdown menu.
Locate and click on Accessibility in the sidebar.
Scroll down and select Display to view your pointer options.
Find the Pointer section and move the Pointer size slider to the right.
Observe the immediate change in your cursor size across the screen.

blocks.text: Beyond just the size, you can modify the colors of your cursor to make it stand out against different website backgrounds. This is particularly useful if you frequently browse sites with high-contrast themes or dark modes. In the same Accessibility > Display menu, look for Pointer outline color and Pointer fill color. Clicking these opens a color picker where you can select a high-visibility shade, such as bright yellow or neon blue, which can help you track the cursor while reading long articles or editing documents.
Using the Shake to Locate feature

If you prefer to keep your cursor at a standard size but often lose track of it on large displays, the Shake to Locate feature is an excellent alternative. When enabled, this feature causes the pointer to grow significantly in size for a brief moment when you quickly move your mouse or swipe across your trackpad. You can toggle this setting in the Accessibility > Display menu by checking the box next to Shake mouse pointer to locate.

Sometimes, users report that the cursor disappears or fails to change when hovering over links. This is rarely a sign of a broken browser. Instead, it often relates to how websites use CSS to define custom cursor behavior. If you encounter a situation where the hand icon does not appear over a link, try refreshing the page or opening the link in a new tab to reset the browser state.

If you notice that your pointer is not resizing correctly, ensure that you are not running third-party mouse software that might be overriding system settings. Drivers for gaming mice or tools like BetterTouchTool can sometimes interfere with macOS native display scaling. Temporarily disabling these tools can help you determine if they are the source of the conflict.

faq.question: Can I change the cursor size only for Safari?
faq.answer: No, cursor size settings on macOS are system-wide and apply to all applications, including Safari.

faq.question: Does changing the cursor size affect my browser performance?
faq.answer: No, adjusting the pointer size does not impact Safari's speed, memory usage, or general performance.

faq.question: What should I do if the cursor disappears?
faq.answer: If your cursor vanishes, check if you have any third-party mouse drivers running, or try resetting the pointer size slider in System Settings to the default position.
